match.reason: The bank point teaches sperm and egg structure and fertilisation at Year 9 depth, but the new point also requires that each gamete gives half the offspring's chromosomes, which the card does not teach, so it needs a new step rather than a small change.

draft.title: Reproductive cells in animals
card: A sperm cell is small and has a tail, which it uses to swim towards the egg. It carries half of the father's chromosomes.
An egg cell is much larger than a sperm cell and does not swim. It has a store of food for the first stage of the new life, and carries half of the mother's chromosomes.
Fertilisation is when a sperm cell and an egg cell join. The new cell has a full set of chromosomes.
Each parent gives half of the offspring's chromosomes, so the offspring has a mix from both parents.
draft.remember: Small swimming sperm meet a large egg with a food store, and each gives half the chromosomes.

a.q: Why is an egg cell much larger than a sperm cell?
opts: It holds a food store for the early stage of the new life
It needs a large tail so that it can swim to the sperm
It carries all of the offspring's chromosomes by itself
It must be big enough to hold many sperm cells at once
a.why: The egg's size comes from its food store, which supports the new cell after fertilisation. It is not larger because it carries more chromosomes: the egg and the sperm each give half.
a.clue: Think about what the new cell needs just after fertilisation.

b.q: A sperm cell and an egg cell from a pair of kangaroos join in fertilisation. Which statement about the joey's chromosomes is correct?
opts: Half came from each parent, because each cell gave half
All came from the mother, because her egg cell is larger
All came from the father, because his sperm cell swims
Most came from the mother, because her egg has food
b.why: Each reproductive cell carries half of the chromosomes, so the joey gets half from each parent. The egg is larger because of its food store, but size does not mean it gives more chromosomes.
b.clue: Does a bigger cell carry more of the chromosomes?

wants.why: It shows the difference in size and shape between the two cells and how they join.

a.best: It holds a food store for the early stage of the new life
